idiom_name: final class conforming to the protocol with a recorded-calls array
implementation_notes: The collaborator is a protocol and the recording fake is a small conforming type - a Dictionary for state plus an array of typed operation values for the journal, exposed via a private(set) property or a method the test reads; protocol conformance is the ordinary way to implement anything in Swift, so no framework is needed and nothing of the classic structure has to be built. Swift has no built-in mocking framework, and libraries such as Cuckoo or Mockingbird generate mocks with expectations rather than behaviour, so the hand-written journal is the shortest route to interaction assertions. Re-create the fake per test, keep it in the test target, and remember that only the test framework's assertions can fail a test - the double itself never rejects an unexpected call.
pitfalls: A struct fake is copied when installed: the system under test mutates its own copy and the test's journal stays empty - use a final class whenever the collaborator is stored.
Under strict concurrency a fake captured by an async collaborator must be Sendable (or @unchecked with internal locking), otherwise the compiler rejects the test or the array races.
A reference-semantics fake kept in a shared fixture leaks state between tests; re-create it per test.
